title: Episode Fact Ledger
description: Machine-readable per-episode ledger of every externally-checkable claim in a video, its evidence, its on-screen treatment, and its review state. One ledger file per episode. The render gate reads this file; no render ships with an unresolved 'unverified' or 'gate' state.

id.description: EPnnn for a long-form episode, Snnn for a Short. Shorts became first-class deliverables in docs/strategy/slate.md; this schema predated that.

spec_script_sha256.description: Hash of the narration script this ledger was reconciled against. Changing the script invalidates the gate.

narration_source.description: Path or URI of the approved script.

sources.description: Source registry. Facts reference these by id. Keeping sources in one place prevents the same document being cited at two different tiers.

tier.description: Evidence tier, highest first. TIER-1 primary document or patent. TIER-2 contemporary account or institutional archive record. TIER-3 museum catalogue or peer-reviewed secondary. TIER-4 popular secondary book or trade press. TIER-5 encyclopaedic or unsourced web. TIER-6 model-generated: never citeable.

citation.description: Full citation, Chicago-ish. Author, Title (Place: Publisher, Year), page.

archive_url.description: Wayback/archive.today snapshot. Required for any web-only source: links rot and a rotted citation is indistinguishable from a fabricated one.

locator.description: Where in the source the fact sits: page, folio, patent claim, catalogue item number, column.

quote.description: Verbatim excerpt supporting the fact. Required for TIER-1..TIER-3.

facts.description: One entry per externally-checkable claim. A claim stated twice in the script is still one fact, with two narration_spans.

claim.description: The claim in one sentence, as plainly as it can be stated. Written to be falsifiable.

status.description: verified: supported by TIER-1..3. contested: competent sources disagree. unknown: no source establishes it. unsupported: asserted in popular retellings, no evidence found. false: evidence contradicts it. dramatic: a deliberate simplification or composite, declared as such on screen.

counter_evidence.description: Required when status is contested, unsupported or false: what the competing version is and who holds it.

what_would_settle_it.description: Required when confidence is low or status is unknown. The specific document, measurement or experiment that would resolve it.

narration_spans.description: Character or timestamp ranges in the approved script where this claim is voiced. Used to detect a script edit that outruns the ledger.

on_screen.description: How the fact is represented to the viewer. This is where uncertainty becomes a design decision rather than a rhetorical risk.

treatment.description: assert: stated plainly. hedge: stated with an explicit qualifier. range: given as a range, not a point. two_readings: both interpretations shown. show_the_gap: uncertainty named on screen. omit: not stated in narration.

hedge_text.description: Exact words used when treatment is hedge, range, two_readings or show_the_gap. Burned in or spoken.

citation_format.description: On-screen sourcing is a slug (e.g. 'ICE Archives, 1828'), never a full bibliography; the full citation lives in the description and the ledger.

depiction_risk.description: How the accompanying visual was made. 'physically_simulated' must not be presented as 'measured' - see sim_backing.

sim_backing.description: Present only when the shot rests on a solver. Records whether the solver is evidence or illustration.

role.description: illustration: looks right, proves nothing, may not be described as engineering evidence. corroboration: reproduces a documented outcome using sourced parameters. prediction: makes a claim no source makes - requires a stated uncertainty band and is never asserted as fact.

validator_disclaimer.description: The solver vendor's own statement that the tool is not for engineering accuracy, quoted. Required when role is illustration and the shot could be mistaken for analysis.

parameters_source.description: Source ids for every material property fed to the solver. Unsourced parameters make a simulation fiction with numbers on it.

state.description: Only agent_checked and human_approved satisfy the gate. 'blocked' means the script asserts something the ledger will not support.

supersedes.description: Fact id this replaces after a correction. Never delete a corrected fact; retract it forward so the episode's error history stays auditable.

gate.description: The accuracy review gate. A render job may not start unless this block evaluates clean against the ledger contents.

provenance.description: Maps this ledger onto W3C PROV-O so the research trail is queryable and so 'who asserted this and when' survives a handover to another agent.
